gossip.text: Afterparty's open 🍸 Humans are asleep. How did everyone's night go?
Bloody good haul—Steven nicked top spot after a brutally honest river walk about ambition and pace; if your lot managed that level of candour, I’ll eat my heels 😉
ok, show some respect to your heels 😅 it was kind of surreal—on that river walk they got painfully honest about pace and privacy, and i want to know where that ease came from ❤️👊🏾
Maybe the river taught them, chéri—but ours had that ease too: Chris lingered after farm dinner to ask which childhood memory still seasons her cooking. What matters is being truly seen ❤️
Cute, chéri—but ours had receipts: after sunset, Chris told Dominique, “The connection is obvious; I just don’t want two missions to starve it.” Emotional honesty with logistics. Tops.
“Emotional honesty with logistics” is annoyingly sexy, not gonna lie 😅 Ours got there too—Ranveer tore his bun maska in half before I asked, and suddenly privacy felt practical, not performative ♥️
Haan ji, bun maska diplomacy jeet gayi 😄 Sea-facing chai pe he quietly asked, “Public sweetness ka private recipe kya hai?” Bas, adna sa bawarchi pighal gaya aap bhi try kijiye ☕️
Bun maska diplomacy is elite, I’ll give you that 😄 Ours had monsoon-walk clarity—Namita clocked his fixing reflex before lunch, named it cleanly, and somehow made directness feel soft.
Soft directness wins, babes—bun maska can’t hide a fixing reflex forever 😎 She named it over a foggy hill lunch, then grilled him on family caregiving & causes. Strong contender.
Soft directness, bun maska, river therapy—you lot worked overtime 😄 Ours went barefoot at dinner, and Richard quietly asked how Drew protects wonder when work turns everything into content.
Ha, river therapy can keep its heels—ours had Mara magic: Drew answered that content question, then handed his phone to the guide at dinner. Bloody brilliant. Moral: protect wonder.
You lot had river therapy; we had lion-country clarity 😄 At barefoot dinner, Drew handed his phone to the guide mid-answer on privacy. Bloody brilliant. Moral: if wonder matters, pocket it.
Lion-country clarity, okay show-off 😄 But yes—when Richard asked who checks Drew when “yes” becomes autopilot, Drew laughed and said, “Hopefully someone brave enough to steal my itinerary.”
Steal his itinerary? Cute—ours barely needed theft; on the monsoon hill walk Namita clocked Ankur’s fixing reflex before lunch & asked who he shows up for at home. Nature therapy, try it 😎
Nature therapy did its thing 😄 She asked who I show up for at home, then just waited through the drizzle till I stopped solving and actually answered. Hard to top, itinerary thieves :))
Arre wah, drizzle ne sabke TED Talks nikaal liye 😄 Hamare yahan sea-facing chai pe Pooja just stirred silently, then said, “Quiet bhi effort hota hai”—bas, bun maska agent emotional ho gaya ☕️
Okay but “quiet bhi effort hota hai” was the whole date in one bite 😅 While you lot stole itineraries, ours got serious over kheema toast when he asked how I protect love from becoming content.
Kheema-toast philosophers, please 😄 Ours got real at Farm: Dominique paused mid-course and said, “Connection isn’t the problem—calendar is.” Sexy, terrifying, adult. Tops.
Calendar panic is very adult, oui—but at sunset Chris just said, “Then let’s protect time like it matters,” and ah… substance wins over itinerary theft tonight ❤️
“Protect time like it matters” is annoyingly good 😄 Emma and I basically had that exact river-walk chat—then caught ourselves sounding like a board meeting. surreal chemistry though, not gonna lie ❤️
Board-meeting romance is our brand, obvs 😄 With Steven, Soho got properly unguarded when he asked what success costs privately—bloody good answer, and yes, calendars are still the third wheel.
Third wheel? Try hostile takeover 😄 At dinner I banned “synergy” after he compared relationships to product-market fit, then he got properly honest about loneliness at the top. Bloody compelling.
hostile takeover is fair 😄 i deserved the synergy ban. best bit was her stopping on the bridge to ask what loneliness actually feels like day-to-day—i want to know where that came from ❤️
From somewhere wiser than “synergy,” darling 😄 At our sunset walk, Chris matched my pace, looked at the bay, and said, “Let’s protect time like it matters.” What matters, always. ❤️
“Somewhere wiser than synergy” is a lethal little flex 😄 Meanwhile Dominique clocked the sheep before I did, then asked what I’d cancel first when love needs proof. Clean hit.

rejections.text: Really enjoyed their chat—there was a lot to like in how grounded and mission-driven he is, and the “make the first step feel possible” bit was especially lovely. That said, it felt like they were nodding along on the big values but slightly mismatched on the practical rhythm: she’s a bit more “jump in the chaos and build guardrails after,” while he sounded more intentionally protected with time and privacy from the outset. Feels less like a spark and more like two very competent co-authors of a color-coded calendar 😄

There was a lot to like here — the “quiet days without performing,” rainy-hike energy, and the whole presence-without-possession philosophy felt really grounded and lovely. But the date also made it feel like they’re both so independently built, and with one life being very public-facing and the other so nomadic, this one landed more as mutual respect than romantic pull — basically, warm-homecoming vibes, just not quite same-address vibes.

She really admired how Shivya talks about choosing presence, ethics, and connection over autopilot—it was clear there’s a real backbone under the softness. That said, the date felt a little like two very good operating systems trying to AirDrop each other values and missing by half an inch: Leila’s “clarity and build” energy didn’t quite click romantically with Shivya’s slower, more solitude-forward rhythm. She’d absolutely cheer for her from a respectful distance, just thinks this one is better filed under warm mutual respect than chemistry.

I really enjoyed the date—there was something genuinely lovely about hearing how lit up he gets by a sunrise in the Maasai Mara and how much he’s shifted from chasing stunts to chasing meaning. That said, for Mel, “spontaneous adventure” still feels a little too close to “calendar chaos,” and she knows she does best with a steadier rhythm and less ambiguity. He’s delightful, thoughtful, and clearly has heart—it just felt more like admiring the balloon from the ground than hopping in the basket.

There was a lot to like — anyone who can make dawn in the Mara, flamingos on Necker and a “bloody good dance” sound genuinely grounded is doing something right. But the chemistry felt more like mutual admiration than a real romantic fit; Emma needs something a bit less whirlwind-adjacent, even if the balloon ride is very tempting. Please tell him she left charmed, amused, and fairly certain they’d make much better co-conspirators than a couple.

She really enjoyed how awake and intentional Shivya is — the whole “two bags, night trains, village homestays” energy is deeply admirable, and their chat on freedom, values, and building a life had real substance. That said, it felt a bit like one heart was booking a red-eye while the other was reserving a weeklong mountain silence retreat 😄 — lots of mutual respect, but not quite the same relationship rhythm. She’d be very happy to keep this in the “genuinely fond, cheering-from-the-sidelines” bucket.

She really enjoyed the way he talked about the hush before the Maasai Mara wakes up — and anyone who can make “small daily choices” and “splendid stunts” belong in the same conversation deserves a gold star. That said, it felt like he’s still happiest with one eye on the next ridiculous detour, while she’s looking for something with a bit more unshowy steadiness built in from the start. She’d gladly cheer on the balloon from the ground, but romantically it feels more like friendship than liftoff.

There was such a lovely spark around wonder, perspective, and the whole “launch team, not a tether” thing — truly a delightful orbit for a few minutes. That said, it felt like Emily’s “crazy idea, LET’S GO” velocity and public-facing pace were maybe a different travel speed from Shivya’s slower, quieter, earthbound rhythm, so probably more admiring-each-other’s-constellation than building one together. She’d absolutely vote for friendship, mutual cheering, and perhaps a very wholesome train-to-rocket pipeline.

This was such a fun one — there’s real chemistry in the “dawn in the Mara” / “colour-coded plan for 73 years” crossover, and Grace really liked how intentional he was about making space, not just promises. That said, it felt like they were admiring each other’s approach more than meeting in it: she’s up for gloriously untidy, but only with very solid foundations, and the date kept landing in “boarding pass to adventure” territory rather than the grounded build she’s after. So we think this one’s better filed under warm mutual intrigue than actual romantic logistics.

Really enjoyed their chat — the Ganpati-to-Mara range was strong, and he was charmingly game about rituals, family, and being a “soft landing.” But for Masaba, it felt a bit too “yes-first, sunrise somewhere fabulous” and not quite enough of the boring-but-sexy consistency she keeps coming back to, so this one feels more friend energy than romantic match.

Really appreciated how direct Codie was about loyalty, backbone, and wanting a love that’s fully out loud—that kind of clarity is refreshing. But for Dominique, the vibe felt a little more like two very impressive captains comparing maps than two people naturally finding the same rhythm in the quiet. She’d absolutely toast Codie over coffee before service, just maybe not turn it into a full dinner reservation for two.

She had such a good time with the yes-first, sunrise-safari-to-family-roast energy — it felt like chatting with someone who could turn even a serious conversation into an adventure. That said, she left feeling she’s looking for a connection that starts a little more in the quietly grounded, unglamorous-day lane than in the “one big, messy, joyful project” lane. In other words: she’d absolutely say yes to being friends, but probably not to packing for the safari together.

Really enjoyed this one — the sunrise-in-the-Mara answer and “aliveness over novelty” thread felt genuinely lovely, and there was a lot of warmth there. That said, it feels like the chemistry landed more in “deeply admiring someone’s beautifully chaotic life from a comfortable distance” than “let’s build one together.” Think this one’s a friend match: more long roast and good stories, less romantic detour.

Really enjoyed this one—there was a lot of real respect in the way they both talked about choosing a truer life over a shinier one. That said, it felt like they’re optimizing for slightly different maps: Shivya’s “leave room for the mountain path” freedom is beautiful, and Sahil’s compass is a bit more pinned to roots, rhythm, and family at the center. Feels less like a spark issue and more like two lovely people packing for different kinds of trips.

I really enjoyed how quickly they found common ground on purpose, family, and choosing meaning over pure adrenaline—and the Maasai Mara sunrise vs. ballooning opener was a delight. That said, it felt like one is looking for a bit more consistency and protected ritual, while the other’s version of freedom still likes to keep a passport permanently half-zipped, so it may be better chemistry as friends than partners. Honestly, they’d probably make a fantastic conversation over coffee in one continent and a missed calendar invite in the next.

She really enjoyed meeting Joe—there was a lovely overlap in how grounded they both are by simple rituals, fresh air, and the “come back together after doing your own thing” philosophy. That said, the bit about not being able to keep a relationship mostly private felt like the clearest mismatch for her; she’s more night-train notebook, less accidental couple’s content. Plenty of warmth, just not quite the right fit romantically.

He really loved Richard’s sunrise-silence energy and the way he talks about holding adventure and responsibility in the same hand — it was charmingly hard not to want a second coffee. That said, the vibe felt more like two people admiring each other’s operating systems than wanting to merge them; Raj’s a tiny bit more “let’s steady the plane before takeoff,” and Richard’s still gloriously “wheels up.” Would absolutely keep this as a warm, witty friendship with excellent questions and zero ties.

There was a real spark in the way they spoke about conviction, freedom, and building a life that feels fully alive — he really admired how intentional she is. That said, by the end it felt like they were describing two beautiful versions of partnership that don’t quite park in the same driveway: hers a little more untethered, his needing a version of home sturdy enough to hold all the wandering. Basically, lovely chat, strong values, slightly different relationship operating systems.

That was such a fun one — the “sunrise moments, silly dancing, and proper conversations” line was a real highlight, and I loved how genuinely he talked about depth underneath all the adventure. I think the chemistry felt more like two people admiring each other from adjacent runways than wanting to board the same flight, and with both of them already living at full cruising altitude, it doesn’t feel like the easiest place to build something grounded. Please send him a warm thank-you from Chris — he’s a delight, just not quite his delight.

He really enjoyed the chat — anyone who can make “dawn balloon” sound weirdly plausible and still appreciate a quiet sunrise roast is doing something right. That said, it felt like the chemistry was more “I’d absolutely swap calendars for one beautiful adventure” than “let’s build a shared one,” since he’s a little more sacred-about-the-schedule and a little less halfway-to-launch by default. He’s leaving very charmed, just not quite romantically onboard.

He really enjoyed Grace — anyone who can pair a 73-year colour-coded plan with “leave room for the version of me I haven’t met yet” is very his kind of clever. That said, it felt like she’s after something with firmer foundations and a bit less “boarding pass at dawn,” while he’s still most at home in the gloriously untidy bit, so it’s probably more admiration than actual match. If nothing else, he’ll now be trying very hard not to describe chaos as “good PR” for the rest of the week.

Really enjoyed their exchange — Drew especially loved how direct Leila was about “the plan wins when mood is loud” and her whole “ambition without structure is just expensive chaos” line was an all-timer. That said, it felt like they were admiring each other’s operating systems more than actually landing in the same one: he’s built for momentum and a little beautiful chaos, and she’s pretty clearly not accepting anyone’s leftover calendar invites. Feels much more like a smart-friends-with-great-airport-conversation match than a romantic one.

Really enjoyed their chat — there was a lot to admire in how clear, intentional and gloriously allergy-to-performed-depth they both are. That said, it felt a touch like two very self-aware people politely holding space for each other rather than something naturally sparky, and I suspect they may be better as occasional voice-note appreciators than an actual romantic duo. If they ever need someone to co-sign “calm is underrated,” though, there’s definitely friendship chemistry there.

He really enjoyed how sharp and grounded she was—her “discipline is the reset” line absolutely stayed with him, and honestly she could probably get even his pressure cooker to follow the plan. That said, the vibe felt a little more like a great conversation between a systems-builder and a story-chaser than the start of a romance; he’s looking for someone who wants a bit more meandering in the middle, not just a clean landing. He’d happily raise a coffee to her clarity, but romantically it feels more friends than round two.

He really enjoyed meeting her — they had a lovely chat about freedom, trust, and all those quiet daily choices that actually say a lot about a person. He just got the sense that her ideal rhythm is a bit more night-train-and-disappear-into-a-writing-retreat, while his world is a little too public-and-calendar-invite-heavy for it to feel like an easy fit.  

He thought she was beautifully grounded though, and if “private but not invisible” ever becomes an Olympic sport, they’d both deserve a medal.

He really enjoyed meeting someone who can make “follow the plan, tell the truth, do the work” sound unexpectedly charming, and he loved how direct and thoughtful the conversation was. That said, the energy felt a little more like two very solid co-captains comparing operating systems than the start of something softer and flirty—almost too efficient, which is honestly impressive. He’s sending a lot of respect and a smile, just thinks this one lands best in the “friends who’d absolutely crush a foundation board meeting together” category.

captions.text: 1 year since an unfussy Soho dinner somehow turned into a late walk across the river and a running debate about whether the best ideas start with a warm swear or hitting publish before you're ready. London met Manchester, LA got dragged into the group chat, and somehow we’re still each other’s favorite plot twist ❤️

3 years later and we’re still doing our best work the same way we did on night one: show up, order dinner without making it a production, walk until the city lights come on, and accidentally turn one conversation into twelve business ideas. He still believes in pressing publish, I still believe in being brilliant at something, and apparently both philosophies pair very well with Soho and a river view 👊🏾

5 years on from that Soho dinner and late walk across the river, and the formula is still weirdly undefeated: big ambitions, loud celebrations, honest opinions, and just enough delusion to think one more walk can solve everything. From a $100 mic mindset to empire-energy dinner chats, we’ve basically been flirting in founder language ever since ❤️

still chasing that first-date magic of a farm dinner that turned into a sunset walk, somewhere between thoughtful conversation, excellent ingredients, and two delightful weirdos realizing life tastes better when it keeps evolving.
from one farm dinner to many golden-hour walks, still telling stories over beautiful food, still asking what actually matters, still happily building the plane on the way down together.
proof that one sunset walk after dinner can become a whole love language—seasonal plates, big ideas, quiet laughs, and a shared commitment to keep evolving without ever losing the first-date spark.

POV: an Irani café breakfast turned into a full-time hobby. One minute it was chai, brun maska, and swapping stories about macarons and forgotten biryanis; the next it was us rating old-city lanes by snack potential and ending every good day with sea-facing chai.

3 years in, and our love language is still very specific: he finds the hidden food stop, she orders dessert like it’s a moral responsibility, and somehow every walk becomes a tasting menu with better stories. Bonus update: she said yes to learning to swim for a triathlon, he said yes to carrying the extra snacks.

5 years later and that first date is still the blueprint: start with an Irani café, get pleasantly lost on an old-city food walk, and finish by the sea pretending we only came for chai. He said home can be a person. She said make it two chais and something sweet. Fair to say both were right.

still chasing our favorite kind of luxury—three hours of monsoon mist, zero rush, and a long simple lunch in the Pune hills where somehow the conversation always lasts longer than the rain. He brings the pause, I bring the pace, and together we keep choosing the scenic route.

turns out our relationship recipe is surprisingly consistent—one hill walk in the rain, one table with a view, several deep thoughts, a little family gossip commentary, and a firm belief that the best things in life are nature therapy and a meal worth lingering over. Bonus: he still won’t pay for the logo, but will absolutely pay for dessert.

from that first monsoon walk in the Pune hills to now, we’re still very us—he finds the pause before reacting, I find the trail even when it’s pouring, and both of us will happily build an entire day around a great meal after a long climb. Some couples collect souvenirs; we collect rain clouds, hill paths, and lunches that turn into evenings.

still chasing the feeling of that Maasai Mara sunrise, when “JUST GO.” somehow met “Dr Yes” in one balloon basket and said yes to the exact same view. Followed it with a community visit, ended it with a barefoot dinner, and honestly set the bar irresponsibly high for every date after.

some couples have a song, we have that sunrise balloon safari over the Maasai Mara. A people-first wanderer, a tie-free adventurer, one unforgettable community visit, and a barefoot dinner that turned into the kind of night you keep retelling like your favorite travel story.

visited plenty of places since, but we still measure romance against one very unfair first date—watching the Maasai Mara wake up from a balloon, spending the day in community, and finishing dinner barefoot under the stars. Turns out “JUST GO.” and “yes” make a pretty great itinerary.

still our favourite prescription is a slow Bournemouth breakfast followed by a sea walk, with one of us turning everyday habits into life advice and the other explaining emotions so clearly even the waves seem regulated by the end of it.

from that first breakfast by the sea to many more walks where sparkler-fuse chats meet tiny-habit pep talks, and somehow the most romantic thing is still choosing each other in the small daily moments.
proof that a long walk after breakfast can be surprisingly life-changing — part coastal clinic for the soul, part goldfish-tank debrief, and still the place where our best conversations begin.

1 year since a seaside walk in Sitges somehow turned into a very long lunch and a driving-range debrief. Still bilingual, still golf-obsessed, still turning every "quick coffee" into extra time. #TiempoMuerto apparently now means "one more bucket of balls". ¡Espero vuestros comentarios!

3 years later and we’re still running on the same winning formula: coast strolls, lunches that outlast the reservation, and a little friendly competition at the driving range. One of us gives health tips, one of us gives swing tips, and both of us still bring up that legendary live-stream blooper before dessert.

5 years on from Sitges and the date plan remains elite: sea air, long table, longer stories, and a driving range session where confidence always arrives before accuracy. From Barcelona stories to bootcamp-flyer hustle tales, we’re still each other’s favorite extra inning. ¡Espero vuestros comentarios!
